guarantees.claim: u_aes_dom_inverse_gf2p4 is wired to permanently drive a_theta, b_theta, prd_o.prd_2, prd_o.prd_3 from a_gamma_buf, b_gamma_buf, prd_i.prd_2, prd_i.prd_3; internal computation updates only when we_i[2:1] enables it.
guarantees.cond: always (static connection); internal device logic controlled by we_i[2:1]

guarantees.claim: u_prim_flop_ab_y10_qqq registers the 16-bit vector {a_y1, a_y0, b_y1, b_y0} on clk_i when we_i[2] is high, and drives a_y1_qqq, a_y0_qqq, b_y1_qqq, b_y0_qqq.

u_aes_dom_mul_theta_y1 drives a_y_inv[3:0] and b_y_inv[3:0] with the masked multiplication of a_y1_qqq and a_theta (share a) and b_y1_qqq and b_theta (share b), reshared with prd_i.prd_4[7:4], when we_i[3] is high.

u_aes_dom_mul_theta_y0 drives a_y_inv[7:4] and b_y_inv[7:4] with the masked multiplication of a_theta and a_y0_qqq (share a) and b_theta and b_y0_qqq (share b), reshared with prd_i.prd_4[3:0], when we_i[3] is high.

assumptions.claim: The external controller must sequence we_i such that we_i[2:1] enables the inverse before we_i[2] captures y1/y0 into flops, and we_i[3] enables the multipliers after the inverse has produced stable a_theta/b_theta.
assumptions.risk: If we_i[3] is asserted before we_i[2] or we_i[2:1] is asserted out-of-order, the multipliers may use uninitialized or stale a_theta/b_theta or qqq values, leading to functionally incorrect masked outputs.

assumptions.claim: prd_i.prd_2, prd_i.prd_3, and prd_i.prd_4 must deliver fresh, independent random values when the corresponding enables (we_i[2:1] for prd_2/prd_3, we_i[3] for prd_4) are active.
assumptions.risk: Non-random or correlated randomness can break the masking scheme, enabling side-channel leakage of secret processed data.

assumptions.claim: Inputs a_y1, a_y0, b_y1, b_y0 must hold stable values at the rising edge of clk_i when we_i[2] is high.
assumptions.risk: Glitches or set-up/hold violations can cause the flops to capture corrupted data, leading to wrong multiplication inputs and incorrect downstream results.

uncertain_points.claim: The inverse instance u_aes_dom_inverse_gf2p4 receives we_i[2:1] as its we_i port (2‑bit vector). The meaning of these two bits (e.g. separate stage enables) inside the inverse module is unknown.
uncertain_points.risk: If the inverse expects a different bit assignment or a single-bit enable, the enable gating may be incorrect, causing the inverse to operate at wrong times or not at all.
